data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: drop the hardcoded hand tcp offset from the duo moveit config too

The mobile fr3 duo moveit config declares the same tcp_xyz:='0 0 0.1034' as the
two description extensions, and it accepts ee_id, so a pump mounted through it
was placed at the franka hand's offset like the others. Found by generating
every franka_ros2 entry point that builds a franka_description robot against
the resolved default: this file was the only remaining one that still forced
the hand's value.

Verified by expanding it with a pump before and after: 0 0 0.1034 becomes the
pump's own 0 0 0.105, while the franka hand stays at 0 0 0.1034. The franka_ros2
suite reports the same 35 pre-existing failures with and without the change.

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: Kamal Mohy El Dine
data.message:
fix: let the mounted end effector decide the tcp offset

Both description extension entry points hardcoded the franka hand's
0 0 0.1034, so a robot built from them with ee_id:=cobot_pump placed the
pump's tcp 1.6 mm off, at the hand's offset rather than the pump's own
0 0 0.105. Leaving tcp_xyz empty hands the decision to the end effector,
which is where the offset is actually defined.

Depends on the franka_description change that resolves an empty tcp_xyz;
against a franka_description without it an empty tcp_xyz reaches the end
effector verbatim and emits an empty origin, so this must not merge first.

Signed-off-by: Kamal Mohy El Dine <kamal.mohy@franka.de>

data.author: kuhn_an
data.message:
fix(franka_bringup): exclude passive joints from TMR hardware interfaces

tmrv0_2_ros2_control documents passive base joints (rocker, casters,
optional spine) as simulation-only, with real hardware exposing only
the four drive joints. franka_bringup/urdf/tmrv0_2.urdf.xacro is the
common bringup entry point for both real hardware and mock/fake
hardware testing, so its include_passive_base="true" contradicted that
contract: both real and mock TMR bringup now register exactly the four
drive joints on the ros2_control hardware interface.

franka_gazebo_bringup/urdf/tmrv0_2.gazebo.urdf.xacro is unaffected: it
is an independent entry point that sets include_passive_base="true" at
its own call site, so the Gazebo TMR remains at nine joints (four drive
+ five passive base joints). This aligns tmrv0_2 with
franka_bringup/urdf/mobile_fr3_duo.urdf.xacro and with the MoveIt
config, which already gate the flag on simulate_in_gazebo.

The global /joint_states topic (joint_state_publisher) is unaffected by
the four-joint hardware surface: joint_state_publisher back-fills the
passive joints declared in the URDF that are absent from the
ros2_control-published /franka/joint_states, so the aggregate
/joint_states and the TF tree still carry all URDF joints.

Extend controller_service_client with list_hardware_interfaces() and
fake_hardware_test_base's wait_for_joint_states() with a topic override
to pin the new contract with regression coverage on the fake-hardware
TMR launch test: the ros2_control state interfaces and the
/franka/joint_states topic must expose exactly the four drive joints and
no passive base joint, while the aggregate /joint_states keeps
reporting all URDF joints via back-fill.

data.author: kuhn_an
data.message:
fix: keep broadcasters active through a franka::ControlException (BFFTRAC-2766)

On a franka::ControlException, read() previously returned
return_type::ERROR, which errors the hardware component out and tears
down robot_state_broadcaster and joint_state_broadcaster along with it,
forcing an operator to reactivate them by hand after every reflex.

Latch the fault in control_fault_latched_ instead:
- read() returns OK without refreshing the state buffer while the fault
  is latched, so the component takes the clean INACTIVE lifecycle path
  instead of erroring out, and the state broadcasters keep publishing the
  frozen last-valid telemetry (position/velocity/effort, elbow, pose,
  F/T sensor).
- write() returns DEACTIVATE while the fault is latched, driving the
  controller_manager's self-deactivation path.
- on_activate() refuses with FAILURE on two independent grounds: while the
  control-fault latch is still set, and — defensively, before the latch
  check can be trusted — whenever the last-known robot state reports
  ROBOT_MODE_REFLEX or non-empty current_errors. Either way activation
  before the robot error is cleared reports FAILURE instead of a false
  SUCCESS.
- A franka::NetworkException is not a control fault: read() and write()
  both still return ERROR for it and take the existing
  error/deactivate-broadcasters path, unlatched.

Also drop the duplicate blocking stopRobot() call from read()'s catch
block: on_deactivate() already stops the robot, so the ~2s braking wait
was being paid twice per reflex in the 1 kHz control cycle.

Observable sequence on a reflex: one controller-manager update cycle may
still publish the pre-fault/frozen sample right after read() latches
(broadcasters remain lifecycle-active); the controller_manager then
transitions the hardware component to inactive and runs the deactivation
callback inline, which blocks that update thread for the ~2s braking
stop — controller updates and topic publication are expected to pause
for that duration, and cycle-overrun warnings during this one-time step
are accepted. After the block, inactive-state reads resume and publish
the live reflex state until the robot error is cleared and only the
command controller needs re-activating.

Pin the new contract with regression coverage at both levels: unit tests
for read()/write() returning OK/DEACTIVATE on a ControlException and
ERROR on a NetworkException from either read() or write(), exported
state staying frozen at the last successful read while the fault is
latched, activation failing both while latched and while the buffered
robot state reports reflex/active errors, and succeeding once recovered;
plus a no-hardware launch test that pins the upstream
deactivate_controllers_on_hardware_self_deactivate contract so a hardware
write() DEACTIVATE does not have to take state broadcasters down with it.

Update franka_hardware's error-recovery guide and changelog to match.

Authored-by: AI Assistant

data.message:
Harden no-hardware test suite: isolation, hermetic deps, honest failures

Test isolation & correctness:
- Run controller-activation-order, teleop, and MoveIt planning-smoke launch
  tests under run_test_isolated.py so their move_group/controller_manager/topic
  graphs cannot collide with other packages tested in parallel.
- Check controller [ERROR] output in @post_shutdown_test classes (full run
  output, incl. shutdown) instead of active test methods that only saw partial
  output; share the logic via collect_unexpected_error_lines and ignore benign
  shutdown-race errors (service call timed out, pal_statistics publisher thread).

Hermetic builds:
- Declare direct test deps that were relied on transitively: ament_index_python
  and python3-yaml (franka_bringup, franka_fr3_moveit_config); launch, launch_ros,
  launch_testing, rclpy, sensor_msgs (franka_gazebo_bringup); ament_cmake_ros
  (franka_fr3_moveit_config).
- test_launch_file_parsing now skips packages absent from isolated builds rather
  than failing, while still covering every launch file in full-workspace CI.

CI honesty:
- Gazebo stage reports test/infra failures as UNSTABLE (catchError + non-empty
  junit) instead of hiding them behind '|| true'.

Robustness:
- gazebo_test_utils no longer pkills controller_manager/robot_state_publisher
  (launch_testing owns their lifecycle) and drops the tearDownClass kill that
  raced launch shutdown and could mask exit codes.
- franka_gazebo_hardware guards the gz_ros2_control-system include target with a
  configure-time existence check that fails loudly if the target is renamed.
- Use time.monotonic() for timeout loops; correct README test-framework and
  config-file descriptions.

Redundancy cleanup:
- test_fake_hardware_tmr inherits FakeHardwareTestBase instead of reimplementing
  the ROS lifecycle and wait_for_joint_states.
- Remove test_load_cartesian_impedance_example_controller.cpp; its load
  assertion is already covered by test_load_all_example_controllers.

Verified in the Jazzy container: ament_flake8 clean; libfranka_gz_hardware_plugins.so
carries no DT_NEEDED on the gz plugin libs; fake-hardware, controller-order,

- FR3 Duo: dual-arm controller activation + 14-joint verification
- Mobile FR3 Duo: hardware activation + arm joint presence

feat: Add robot model and robot_state support to Gazebo sim

Bring model and robot_state support to the Gazebo simulation so
model-consuming controllers (model_example_controller), the
gravity_compensation controller, and Cartesian pose/impedance
controllers work in sim for the single fr3 arm (PRCUN-6376).

Rename the Gazebo HW decorator GazeboGravityCompensationSystem to
FrankaGazeboHardwareInterface (class, files, pluginlib id and the
ros2_control <plugin> ids in franka_arm/fr3_duo/mobile_fr3_duo) to
reflect its broadened role. It now builds libfranka's offline
franka::Model each cycle and exports a faithful franka::RobotState,
mirroring the real FrankaHardwareInterface:

* robot_model and robot_state interfaces;
* six _tcp force/torque interfaces so gravity_compensation can
  activate;
* the 16 cartesian_pose_state interfaces so Cartesian pose/impedance
  controllers can activate.

The estimated external wrench is derived from the measured-torque
residual and reported in both the base frame (O_F_ext_hat_K) and the
stiffness frame K (K_F_ext_hat_K and the _tcp interfaces), following
libfranka's reaction-sign convention: a push in +x reads a measured
external force of -x.

Model/robot_state/force-torque export degrades gracefully for
robot_types without a single-arm model (e.g. the dual-arm
mobile_fr3_duo), leaving gravity-comp/passthrough behavior unchanged;
a genuinely missing franka_description or a failed model build is
still logged as an error.

Wire model_example_controller into franka_gazebo_controllers.yaml,
re-enable the gravity_compensation Gazebo launch test with a

data.message:
feat: replace std::mutex with prio_inherit_mutex in franka_hardware for RT safety (PRCUN-6249)

Replace std::mutex with realtime_tools::prio_inherit_mutex for control_mutex_
in both FrankaHardwareInterface and Robot classes. This provides:
- PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT: prevents priority inversion in the 1kHz RT loop
- PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK: detects deadlocks at runtime
- PTHREAD_MUTEX_ROBUST: recovers gracefully if holder thread dies

Fix Robot::getCurrentState() to return franka::RobotState by value instead
of const reference. The previous implementation returned a reference to
current_state_ after releasing the lock, creating a data race where callers
(PTP motion handler from a non-RT thread) could read stale/torn data while
the RT thread mutates current_state_ via readOnce().

Refactors Gazebo gravity overrides for robots

Extracts gravity override configurations for Franka arms and mobile bases into a reusable `gravity_overrides.xacro` file. This centralizes the logic to disable gravity on specific links and apply implicit spring damping where necessary.

Updates launch files to utilize a consolidated `franka_arm.gazebo.xacro` for arm descriptions, which now includes the arm-specific gravity overrides.

These changes prevent robot arms from collapsing in Gazebo simulations when using example controllers that do not implement gravity compensation. The refactoring improves maintainability and reduces duplication across various robot configurations.

Renames the mobile duo launch file to `gazebo_mobile_fr3_duo_example.launch.py` for clarity.

Clarifies instructions for launching the mobile FR3 duo example in Gazebo:
- Sets default launch to exclude sensors for simpler initial setup.
- Provides explicit steps for building `franka_mobile_sensors` and launching with the full sensor suite.
- Introduces a new `world` argument to allow specifying custom SDF world files.
- Updates the list of required `colcon build` packages for a complete setup.

Relates to PRCUN-5966
